title: IaC Guardian: CI gating and OPA policy enforcement for Private/VPC Terraform
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a hardened CI pipeline ("IaC Guardian") for all Private/VPC Terraform repos that enforces linting, produces safe plan artifacts, and blocks unsafe changes via OPA/Conftest policy checks before any apply. This pipeline must be usable by platform engineers and customer on-prem teams and must work with our private state backends and self-hosted agents.
details:
Scope and requirements:
- Run steps on pull requests against all terraform modules used for Private deployments (networking, bastion, cluster bootstrap, kms integration).
- Linting: tflint + custom rules; static security scan: tfsec or Checkov; style checks (terraform fmt).
- Plan generation: create a deterministic terraform plan in a build artifact that can be inspected but strips secrets.
- Policy-as-code: evaluate plan JSON using Conftest (OPA) policies stored in org-policy repo. Policies express deny rules (network exposure, public IPs, KMS key policies, VPC peering exceptions) and soft-warning rules (costly instance types, missing tags).
- Gating model: any deny rule => block merge; warnings => post inline PR comment but allow merge with explicit approver.
- Plan promotion: CI will optionally trigger an apply pipeline that runs in our private Buildkite fleet (agents inside customer VPC or in our private infra) to have access to remote state and private endpoints. Applies require explicit approval for any change that modifies security-sensitive resources.
- Post-apply health checks: smoke test endpoints, validate route tables, verify KMS key policies, and run a lightweight reconciliation check to detect immediate drift. If health checks fail, create an incident runbook and mark the rollout as failed.
- Auditing: record policy evaluations, plan artifacts, policy versions, and who approved applies to a central audit bucket (encrypted).
- Integrations: GitHub PR comments with structured plan summary, Slack channel alerts for fails, and dashboarding in Console (rollout health + last successful plan per module).
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
Key tradeoffs discussed:
- Run Conftest in PR vs pre-commit: PR-level gives a single authoritative run with full plan JSON; pre-commit is faster locally but can be bypassed. We will require both (pre-commit for dev ergonomics, CI Conftest as authoritative gate).
- GitHub Actions vs Buildkite: choose hybrid model — GitHub Actions for fast, ephemeral checks (lint, fmt, tfsec) and to create plan artifacts; Buildkite self-hosted runners inside the private network for plan/apply that need access to private state and keys. This keeps developer feedback fast while preserving network access for apply.
- Where to store policies: central org-policy repo versioned semantically. Policies referenced by commit hash in pipeline to ensure reproducible gating.
- Policy enforcement granularity: deny-by-default for security-sensitive rules; configurable allowlists per-customer via market config file loaded at policy-eval time.
implementation_tasks: Add GitHub Actions workflow 'iac-guardian-pr' to infra and modules repos
Implement Conftest OPA policy library in https://github.com/redwood-inference/org-policy
Add Buildkite pipeline 'iac-guardian-apply' running on private agents with approval step
Enhance terraform-plan job to produce sanitized plan JSON and mask secrets
Add post-apply healthcheck job and automated rollback trigger on critical failures
Create PR comment integration to post structured plan summary and Conftest results
acceptance_criteria: PR runs lint + tfsec + plan and posts plan artifact to the run
Conftest policies run on plan JSON and deny-rule violations block the merge
Apply pipeline requires manual approval for security-sensitive changes and runs on private agents with access to state
Post-apply health checks run automatically and report status to the Console dashboard
Policy evaluation results and plan artifacts are stored in encrypted audit bucket with policy commit hash recorded
